title: You didn’t do it for God.
paragraphs: You didn’t do it for God.

That thought hits harder than you expected. Because on the surface, everything looked right. The prayer was long. The words were polished. The act was visible. People noticed. Some even said, “You’re so faithful.”
But something in you knew.
You checked who was watching.
You adjusted your tone when others came closer.
You felt a quiet satisfaction—not because God was honored, but because you were seen.
God saw it.
And then Jesus says something that cuts straight through the performance:
“Beware of practicing your righteousness before other people in order to be seen by them, for then you will have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.” — Matthew 6:1
Read that again.
No reward.
Not reduced. Not delayed.
None.
That means it’s possible to do the right thing… for the wrong reason… and walk away empty before God.
This is where most people never look.
Because the action feels safe to examine. The motive does not.
You give—but you replay who noticed.
You serve—but you compare your sacrifice to others.
You post something “for encouragement”—but you keep checking the response.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God is not impressed by what you do publicly if your heart is privately feeding on human approval.
The Pharisees mastered this. They fasted, gave, prayed—but Jesus exposed them with terrifying clarity:
“Truly, I say to you, they have received their reward.” — Matthew 6:2
That applause you wanted?
That recognition?
That subtle nod of admiration?
That’s all you get.
And it fades fast.
Because the deeper issue isn’t behavior—it’s worship.
You weren’t just doing something good.
You were seeking something else as your reward.
You were asking people to give you what only God can.
And you knew.
There was that moment—right before you acted—when you felt the pull. That internal shift. That quiet negotiation:
“If they see this, it will mean something about me.”
That’s where it turned.
That’s where righteousness became performance.
And performance is exhausting, because it never satisfies. You need more visibility. More validation. More moments to prove something you’re afraid isn’t real.
So you keep doing “good things”…
But your soul stays restless.
Because it was never about the act.
It was about the audience.
Jesus doesn’t just expose this—He redirects it:
“But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.” — Matthew 6:3
That’s not about secrecy for the sake of it.
That’s about purity of desire.
A heart so focused on God that it forgets to perform.
A soul that is satisfied being seen by Him alone.
Because here’s the truth underneath all of this:
You don’t actually believe God’s approval is enough.
That’s the real fracture.
That’s the hidden motive behind so many “holy” actions.
You want something you can see.
Something immediate.
Something measurable.
But the Gospel confronts that completely.
Because Jesus didn’t come to create better performers.
He came to rescue people whose hearts were addicted to being seen.
“For they loved the glory that comes from man more than the glory that comes from God.” — John 12:43
That’s not just them.
That’s you.
That’s me.
And that kind of love—misplaced, misdirected—can’t be fixed by trying harder to act sincere.
It has to be replaced.
This is where everything shifts.
Because the same Jesus who exposes your hidden motives… goes to the cross for them.
He sees every impure intention, every moment of spiritual pride, every act done for applause instead of worship—
And He doesn’t walk away.
He absorbs the judgment for it.
“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21
Not perform righteousness.
Become it.
Through Him.
That means you don’t have to manufacture a holy image anymore.
You don’t have to prove anything.
You don’t have to chase visibility to feel valuable.
Because in Christ, you are already fully seen—and fully known—and still fully loved.
That changes how you act in secret.
Because now, the secret place is not empty.
It’s where your Father is.
“And your Father who sees in secret will reward you.” — Matthew 6:4
Not maybe.
Will.
But only when He is actually the one you’re seeking.
So now you’re standing between two paths.
One where you keep performing—subtly, carefully, convincingly—while your heart stays divided.
And one where you let God strip the motive down to nothing but Him.
One gets applause.
The other gets God.
And they are not the same.
Say it plainly.
Confess it.
Even here.
“I was doing it to be seen.”
There’s freedom in dragging hidden motives into the light.
There’s healing in agreeing with God instead of defending yourself.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—to stop performing and start actually walking with Him—stay close.
Follow this journey. Not for content. For correction. For growth. For truth that doesn’t flatter you but transforms you.
